title: standby-evacuation-holdoff-coordinator-and-probing-integration
author: Marta Lopez
release_notes: Introduces a standby evacuation hold-off coordinator to reduce noisy regional failovers; adds synthetic probe integration and new telemetry to detect safe rejoin windows.
description:
Context and motivation: recent incidents showed rapid region-wide evacuations triggered by transient KV pressure and probe flapping. This caused churn and prolonged degraded SLOs for multi-tenant customers. This PR implements a lightweight Standby Evacuation Holdoff Coordinator that: 1) aggregates probe signals and KV pressure heuristics; 2) defers irrevocable tenant evacuation for a configurable holdoff window when probes are noisy; 3) surfaces a rejoin-safe signal to the regional failover conductor. Goals: reduce oscillatory evacuations, avoid unnecessary tenant migration, and provide observability for holdoff decisions.

What changed (high level): commits summarize the implementation and tests. Key behavior: - New coordinator service that listens to region health probes and KV pressure events, produces a per-tenant holdoff decision (HOLD/ALLOW) with TTL semantics. - Synthetic probe integration: injected, short-lived synthetic probes that validate stable latencies before ALLOW. - Backoff policy: exponential holdoff with jitter for repeated flaps. - Telemetry: holdoff_decisions counter, holdoff_duration histogram, probe_consistency gauge, and debug traces when a decision blocks evacuation. - Compatibility: coordinator provides non-blocking advisory API; existing evacuation conductor will consult advisory and escalate only after advisory ALLOW or holdoff expiry.

Design notes: the advisor is purposely advisory so we can fast-rollback. The holdoff window defaults to 8s and is configurable per tenant cohort. Synthetic probes run at most twice during holdoff to prevent probe amplification. We avoid extending global SLO timers; escalation to mandatory evacuation occurs after 3x holdoff windows or when KV saturation exceeds a hard threshold.

Files changed (high level): src/services/evac/holdoff_coordinator.go - core coordinator and TTL store; src/services/evac/probe_integration.go - synthetic probe runner and reconciler; src/runtime/slo/enforcer.rs - small adapter that calls advisory API; pkg/telemetry/metrics.yaml - definitions for new metrics; tests/integration/evac_holdoff_integration_test.py - deterministic integration tests and a new flaky-probe scenario; docs/runbooks/evacuation.md - updated runbook and rollback steps; scripts/deploy/helm/values-evac.yaml - config knobs and defaults.

Commits: ["implement holdoff coordinator and TTL store", "add synthetic probe runner and reconcile loop", "adapter in slo enforcer to consult advisory API", "integration tests for probe flapping scenarios", "docs and telemetry definitions"].

Tests and CI: unit tests and lints passed on first run. Integration suite initially failed two flaky tests related to timing assumptions; fixed by using a deterministic clock interface in the tests and re-ran CI. E2E smoke ran in staging and validated that evacuation is skipped under transient probe failures and that eventual evacuations still proceed under sustained KV pressure. CI summary: build: pass; unit-tests: pass; integration-tests: pass; e2e-staging: pass.

Review conversation (high level): - Asha: "Can we make the per-tenant default holdoff configurable via operator UI and expose a metric for active holdoffs?" Answered: added values-evac.yaml knob and holdoff_decisions metric. - Liam: "Concerned about probe amplification — what's the upper bound on synthetic probes during large-scale incidents?" Reply: synthetic probes capped at 2 attempts per tenant per holdoff; implemented a global probe-rate limiter. - Noah: "Telemetry looks good, but add a trace for decisions that block evacuation for >30s" Actioned: added debug trace event. - Asha: approved after metrics addition; Liam approved after probe-rate limiter added.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: coordinator exposes an advisory HTTP/gRPC endpoint; rollout is phased: feature-flagged off by default, enable for internal canary tenants first, then 10% region traffic, then global. Telemetry and a dashboard will be used to monitor: holdoff_rate, average holdoff duration, subsequent evacuation rate, and SLO windows. Rollback: disable feature flag and the advisory returns ALLOW immediately.

Observability & SLOs to watch: - holdoff_decisions{result=HOLD} - probe_consistency - downstream_evacuation_count (should drop for noisy incidents) - request_latency_p50/p95 (no regressions) - tenant_rebalance_ops (should not spike unexpectedly)

Security and safety: advisory API is authenticated and rate-limited; synthetic probes run with a limited call-path and are traceable in audit logs. No tenant data is persisted by probes.

Related work: references ENG-2873 for incident postmortem and SRE-618 for telemetry dashboard request.

Merge outcome: merged via squash; changelog entry added to release notes.

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] docs updated, [x] telemetry added, [x] feature-flagged rollout config included.

Why this is different: instead of immediate eviction we now have a short, observable, configurable holdoff that uses synthetic validation to avoid noisy evacuations and reduce cross-region churn.
